'''Walker:''' {{legend0|#E6E6E6|30–40%}} {{legend0|#D9D9D9|40–50%}} | title = [[List of governors of Alaska|Governor]] | before_election = [[Mike Dunleavy (politician)|Mike Dunleavy]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Mike Dunleavy (politician)|Mike Dunleavy]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 44.40% {{decrease}} }} {{Elections in Alaska sidebar}} The '''2022 Alaska gubernatorial election''' was held on Tuesday November 8, 2022, to elect the [[List of governors of Alaska|governor of Alaska]]. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor [[Mike Dunleavy (politician)|Mike Dunleavy]] won re-election to a second term, becoming the first [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] governor to be re-elected to a second term since [[Jay Hammond]] in [[1978 Alaska gubernatorial election|1978]] and the first governor, regardless of political affiliation, to be re-elected to a second term since [[Tony Knowles (politician)|Tony Knowles]] in [[1998 Alaska gubernatorial election|1998]].{{Cite news |last=Bohrer |first=Becky |date=November 25, 2022 |title=Mike Dunleavy is 1st Alaska governor reelected since '98 |work=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://apnews.com/article/2022-midterm-elections-business-alaska-bill-walker-acfca581940b7d4045df3f2e13f1538d |access-date=November 25, 2022}} Following voter approval of [[2020 Alaska Measure 2|Ballot Measure 2]] during the [[2020 Alaska elections]], this was the first gubernatorial election in Alaska held under a new election process. All candidates ran in a [[Top-four primary#Alaska|nonpartisan blanket top-four primary]] on August 16, 2022,{{Cite web |title=Alaska Division of Elections, Primary Election Info |url=https://www.elections.alaska.gov/Core/primaryelectioninformation.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220504030110/https://www.elections.alaska.gov/Core/primaryelectioninformation.php |archive-date=May 4, 2022 |access-date=December 10, 2021}} and the top four candidates advanced to the general election.{{Cite news |last=Kitchenman |first=Andrew |date=November 18, 2020 |title=Alaska will have a new election system: Voters pass Ballot Measure 2 |language=en-US |work=[[KTOO (FM)]] |url=https://www.ktoo.org/2020/11/17/alaska-will-have-a-new-election-system-voters-pass-ballot-measure-2/ |url-status=live |access-date=November 18, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118052421/https://www.ktoo.org/2020/11/17/alaska-will-have-a-new-election-system-voters-pass-ballot-measure-2/ |archive-date=November 18, 2020}} In addition to Dunleavy, [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former [[Alaska House of Representatives|state representative]] [[Les Gara]], [[Independent politician|independent]] former governor [[Bill Walker (American politician)|Bill Walker]], and Republican [[Kenai Peninsula Borough, Alaska|Kenai Peninsula Borough]] mayor Charlie Pierce advanced to the general election.{{Cite web |title=Live Alaska Governor Election Results 2022 – NBC News |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-primary-elections/alaska-governor-results |access-date=2022-10-03 |website=www.nbcnews.com}} In the general election, Dunleavy narrowly received the majority of votes in the first round, preventing an [[Instant-runoff voting|instant runoff]]. == Primary election == ===Republican Party=== ====Advanced to general==== *[[Mike Dunleavy (politician)|Mike Dunleavy]], incumbent governor{{Cite web |last=Brooks |first=James |date=August 13, 2021 |title=Alaska Gov.
